battle.name: 維京人突襲不列顛群島
battle.theater: 英格蘭北岸林迪斯法恩島
battle.brief: 793年6月8日，挪威西海岸的維京船隊突襲北諾森布里亞的林迪斯法恩島修道院，掠走金銀聖物，並乘回漲的潮水由海路撤退；諾森布里亞王的追兵只在岸上收回部分財物。卡面的亞述長矛早在亞述國覆亡時便已退出戰場，此處代指北歐長矛：窄葉鐵矛頭配長柄，與圓盾、丹麥斧同為登岸突擊隊的骨架。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 交戰方是北方海掠者與北諾森布里亞的王室—教會體系。進攻方來自挪威西海岸維斯特福爾德一帶，是北歐典型的首領—船隊編制：一位以分贓維繫隨從的酋長率領數艘船，船上編有划槳手、持盾者與矛手，灘頭突擊時由船首小組先行登岸。防守方是北諾森布里亞王國，793 年在位的國王埃達爾烏爾夫自本寧一帶集結軍隊；林迪斯法恩修道院雖無城牆，卻有教會建築、圍院、聖物庫與糧倉，是島上唯一具防衛價值的目標，真正的抵禦依賴王室的追擊而非修道院自身的城防。島上還有皮克特與北方不列顛人的武裝，編年史記載襲擊者在島上曾遭他們攻擊。事件的宗教背景是西歐教會與正推行基督教化的北歐王權之間正在成形的對立，雙方分別以「守教者」與「異教徒」自居。
countriesEn: The two sides were northern sea-raiders and the royal and ecclesiastical system of northern Northumbria. The attackers came from the Vestfold district of the Norwegian west coast, organised in the classic Scandinavian chief-and-ship-band pattern: a war leader who kept his followers loyal by dividing the spoils led a handful of vessels, each manned by oarsmen, shield-bearers and spearmen, with a boarding party ready to strike first from the ship's bow. The defenders were the kingdom of Northumbria: King Eardwulf, reigning in 793, musited his host in the neighbourhood of Bamburgh. Lindisfarne Priory had no curtain wall, but it did have church buildings, an enclosure, a treasury and storehouses, which made it the only thing on the island worth defending; real resistance therefore depended on the royal pursuit rather than on any fortification of the monastery itself. Picts and northern Britons also held armed positions on the island, and the chronicle records that the raiders were attacked by them there. The religious background was the still-forming opposition between the Latin Church of the West and the Scandinavian powers in the process of Christianisation, with each side casting itself as the guardian of the faith and the other as the pagan.
people: 關鍵人物可分三類。進攻方的核心是比約恩（Bjørn），維斯特福爾德的王者，後世編年史家與北歐傳統多以他為 793 年襲擊的統帥；同船者另有北歐王族成員，其具體名分在早期記錄中已不可考。防守方的關鍵是諾森布里亞王埃達爾烏爾夫（Eardwulf，約 729 至 830 年在位），他率軍自本寧追向海峽，雖未能把襲擊者盡數留下，卻依編年史記載收回部分被掠財物。最重要的見證者是林迪斯法恩主教希格伯特（Higbert），他在襲擊中倖存並留下記述，成為後世重建修道院、尋回聖物與推動沿海教堂設防的關鍵人物。學術層面上，編年史家貝達（Bede，673 至 735）在 793 年之前已去世，無法為此役作證；今人對 793 年的了解主要依靠《英格蘭編年史》793 年條，以及後來在修道院內編成的《林迪斯法恩編年史》。艾丹主教於 635 年建院，卡爾特（Cuthbert）的聖髑安葬於此，使這座島嶼同時成為宗教中心與歐洲西部最集中的財富堆積點。
peopleEn: The key figures fall into three groups. At the centre of the attacking side is Bjørn of Vestfold, a king of the Norwegian west coast, whom later chroniclers and Scandinavian tradition generally name as commander of the 793 raid; other members of the Scandinavian royal house travelled in the same ships, though their precise identities are no longer recoverable from the early records. The decisive figure on the defensive side is Eardwulf, king of Northumbria, who reigned from about 729 to 830; he led his host from Bamburgh towards the strait and, though he failed to hold the raiders, the chronicle records that he recovered part of the stolen property. The most important witness is Higbert, bishop of Lindisfarne, who survived the attack and left an account, and who became the key figure in the rebuilding of the priory, the recovery of the shrine's treasures and the fortification of churches along the coast. On the scholarly level, Bede (673–735) had already died before 793 and could not testify about the event; what is known of 793 rests mainly on the entry for that year in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and on the Annals of Lindisfarne, compiled later inside the monastery itself. Aidan founded the priory in 635, and the shrine of Cuthbert lay there, which made the island both a religious centre and one of the richest concentration of wealth in western Europe.
kits: 卡面兵器是亞述長矛，約公元前 900 年的兩河流域裝備：短柄、長刃、配鐵鏃，亞述步兵把它與弓、刀、盾合用，靠密集方陣前推。這件武器在 793 年並不存在——亞述帝國在公元前 7 世紀末已滅亡，亞述長矛退出戰場數千年，本卡以它代表同一類型的長柄矛。戰役中實際使用的是北歐長矛：窄葉形鐵矛頭、木柄長約兩公尺，與圓盾（蒙皮木盾、外緣包鐵並釘金屬鉚釘）、丹麥斧組成登岸小隊的骨架；短柄斧亦可用於砍伐柵欄與破門。防方配備以鐵劍、長矛、斧為主，並有弓供民兵與獵兵使用，國王的追兵帶有馬匹，島上無騎兵可恃。攻方船隊為北歐寬身吃水淺的中型船與較長的尖底船，登岸另用隨船小艇，糧食與淡水自帶，全程無攻城器械，沒有投石機或撞柱可用；島上防禦僅有聖彼得教堂與聖卡爾特教堂的石牆、圍院與木柵，石造堡壘要到 16 世紀才出現。兩軍爭奪的實際標的，是修道院庫房裡的金銀器皿、聖物匣、織物與書冊。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Assyrian spear, a Mesopotamian arm of about 900 BC: a short haft, a long blade, an iron head, carried by Assyrian infantry alongside bow, sword and shield and pushed forward in dense formations. It did not exist in 793 — the Assyrian empire had fallen by the end of the seventh century BC and the Assyrian spear had left the battlefield thousands of years earlier, so the card stands for the same class of long-shafted spear. What was actually used in 793 was the Scandinavian long spear, with a narrow leaf-shaped iron head on a wooden shaft of roughly two metres, forming together with the round shield — a skin-covered wooden disc with an iron rim and metal rivets — and the broad-bladed Danish axe the skeleton of the landing parties; short-handled axes also served for cutting palisades and breaking doors. The defenders were armed with iron swords, spears and axes, with bows for militia and huntsmen, and the king's pursuing force brought horses, while the island itself had no mounted troops to rely on. The attacking fleet consisted of broad, shallow-draught Scandinavian merchant-type hulls and longer keel-built craft, with small boats carried aboard for landing; food and water were carried by the crews, and there was no siege engine of any kind, no artillery and no ram. Island defences were limited to the stone walls, enclosure and timber palisade of the churches of St Peter and St Cuthbert; the stone fortress on the site did not appear until the sixteenth century. The real prize on both sides was what lay in the monastery's storehouses: gold and silver plate, reliquaries, textiles and books.
tactics: 戰術的核心是海峽的潮汐與修道院的儲藏。攻方在 6 月初的西南季風下自挪威西海岸渡海南下，接近英格蘭北岸後選在退潮時段登陸；此時林迪斯法恩與本寧之間的海峽底部露出大片泥沙灘地，潮差達數公尺，登陸艇可以直接擱上灘面。奪灘後，突擊小組以圓盾相扣構成盾牆，長矛自盾縫間前指，斧手在後，攻向圍院與聖彼得教堂的入口；島上沒有城防體系、沒有射孔、沒有能封住街巷的城牆，突擊一旦得手即可直抵寶庫與聖物室。搜索時間被壓得很短，隊伍只挑能搬動、能運上船的金銀器、聖物匣、織物與書冊，其餘留在原處。撤退階段出現全場最關鍵的技術難題：退潮使船隻坐灘，敵軍自北面陸路逼近，襲擊者須以人力與滾木把船重新拖回水中；潮水回漲後船隊得以脫身，隨後在海上按船分贓散去。防守方的戰術近乎追擊：國王軍隊自本寧方向沿陸路與堤道接近，以步兵為主而騎兵極少，島上無壕壘可守，防守方也缺乏把襲擊者困在島上的手段，最終未能完成封鎖。白晝時間長有利搜索，但船隊必須在季節風改變前離開，行動窗口不過數日。
tacticsEn: The heart of the tactics was the tide of the strait and the monastery's stores. The attackers crossed from the Norwegian west coast under the south-westerly winds of early June, and chose to land on a falling tide as they came in sight of the north English coast; at that point the bottom of the strait between Lindisfarne and Bamburgh lay exposed as broad flats of mud and sand, the range of the tide running to several metres, so the landing boats could be set directly onto the beach. Once ashore, the assault parties locked their round shields into a shield wall, spears thrust forward between the shield rims, axe-men behind, and drove at the entrance of the enclosure and the church of St Peter; the island had no defensive system, no arrow slits and no walls capable of sealing a street, so once the blow had landed they could go straight to the treasury and the shrine. The search was kept deliberately short, the crews taking only the silver and gold plate, reliquaries, textiles and books that could be carried and shipped, and leaving the rest where it lay. The retreat brought the most difficult technical problem of the whole action: the falling tide grounded the ships, the enemy was approaching overland from the north, and the raiders had to drag their hulls back into the water by manpower and rollers. When the tide rose again the fleet got clear, and the spoil was then divided among the ships at sea. The defence was essentially a pursuit: the royal host came up from Bamburgh by land and along the causeway, mostly on foot with very few riders, and the island offered no ditch or rampart to hold; the defenders lacked the means to trap the raiders on the island, and no encirclement was completed. The long daylight hours favoured the search, but the fleet had to be away before the winds changed, so the window was a matter of days.
data: 可核對的數字有限，但有幾項足以定出戰役骨架。時間：793 年 6 月 8 日，這一天在 2000 年代初被北歐的史學與文化團體選定為「林迪斯法恩掠奪日」的國際紀念日。距離：林迪斯法恩島距北諾森布里亞海岸約 3 公里，是一座潮汐島，退潮時可步行或驅車經堤道與本寧相通。修道院建於 635 年，聖彼得教堂的主體在 7 世紀落成，島上設施在 793 年已有約一百五十年歷史；艾丹主教的聖物庫與卡爾特聖髑使這裡的貴重物品在歐洲西部名列前茅。兵力：編年史沒有留下任何船數與人數，學界一般只作「十數艘船、數百人」量級的推估，與 865 年才出現、規模遠超的「偉大異教軍」並非同一級別。任期：北諾森布里亞王埃達爾烏爾夫的統治橫跨 729 至 830 年，事件正落在他在位期間，麥西亞的埃塞爾雷德亦於同年去世。前史：785 年西撒克遜的布奧特里克王在丹麥人襲擊韋塞克斯海岸時陣亡，說明北歐掠奪並非自 793 年才開始。往後：875 年另一支北歐縱隊再度洗劫同一座修道院，可見 793 年之後守方並未就此脫險。
dataEn: The verifiable numbers are few, but a few of them are enough to fix the framework of the action. Date: 8 June 793, a day that in the early 2000s was chosen by Scandinavian historical and cultural bodies as the international commemorative day, the Raid on Lindisfarne. Distance: the island of Lindisfarne lies about three kilometres off the north Northumbrian coast, and is a tidal island, connected to Bamburgh by a causeway that could be walked or ridden over at low water. The priory was founded in 635 and the main body of the church of St Peter was completed in the seventh century, so the island's installations already stood about a century and a half old in 793; the shrine built by Bishop Aidan and the body of St Cuthbert placed the wealth of the place among the greatest in western Europe. Strength: the chronicle preserved no number of ships and no number of men, and historians generally work with an order of magnitude of a dozen-odd boats and a few hundred men, a very different scale from the Great Heathen Army that only appeared in 865. Reigns: Eardwulf's rule over Northumbria ran from about 729 to 830, so the event fell squarely within his reign, and Æthelred of Mercia likewise died in the same year. Earlier history: in 785 Beorhtric, king of the West Saxons, was killed when the Danes attacked the coast of Wessex, which shows that Scandinavian raiding did not begin in 793. Later history: in 875 another Scandinavian war-band sacked the same priory all over again, so 793 did not put the defenders permanently out of danger.
cause: 起因有三層。第一層是北歐自身的生計與權力結構：8 世紀末的挪威與丹麥仍以氏族—王權的小型聯盟為主，酋長的權威靠贈禮、土地與戰利品維繫，冬季牧業能提供的資源有限，冬季前後的海上掠奪既能換取穀物、鐵器與俘虜，也能為隨從提供戰功與分成。第二層是目標的選擇：西歐的教會財富高度集中，修道院同時是錢庫、聖物庫與文物庫，而林迪斯法恩建在偏遠潮汐島上，守備薄弱、距王室軍隊的核心區有數日路程，撤退只受潮汐限制，是理想的高風險目標。第三層是宗教政治：北歐諸王自 8 世紀末起陸續與基督教接觸並接受洗禮，9 世紀初的傳教士安斯卡爾更在 Birka 一帶傳教；教會在西歐則呼籲法蘭克與撒克遜諸王保護修道院，於是「守教者」與「異教徒」的對立逐漸成形，搶奪教產在教會的記述中自然被寫成挑釁。另一方面，航海的技術條件也已成熟：北歐人熟悉季風與北大西洋航線，同一時期他們已在愛爾蘭海岸與法蘭克沿海反覆登陸，這次不列顛掠奪並非孤例，而是同一套海上戰術在北海另一處的應用。
causeEn: The causes work on three levels. The first is the subsistence and power structure of the North itself: in the late eighth century Norway and Denmark were still organised as small kinship-and-kingship confederacies, and a chieftain's authority was sustained by gifts, land and plunder, while winter herding could supply only so much; raiding by sea before and after winter could be exchanged for grain, iron and captives, and it gave followers battle honours and a share of the take. The second is the choice of target: church wealth in the West was highly concentrated, and a monastery was at once treasury, reliquary and library, while Lindisfarne stood on a remote tidal island, thinly guarded and several days' march from the royal heartland, its withdrawal limited only by the tide — a high-risk target of ideal shape. The third is religious politics: the Scandinavian kings had begun, from the late eighth century, repeated contact with Christianity and successive baptisms, and in the early ninth century the missionary Ansgar was preaching around Birka; in the West the Church was urging the Frankish and Saxon kings to protect monasteries, so the opposition between the guardians of the faith and the pagans hardened, and the taking of church goods was naturally written up as a provocation. The technical conditions of seamanship were also mature: the Northmen knew the monsoons and the North Atlantic routes and had by this time landed repeatedly on the coasts of Ireland and Frankish lands, so the British raid was not an isolated venture but the same naval warfare applied in another corner of the North Sea.
impact: 793 年此役在後世被定為維京時代的起點，「維京時代 793 至 1066」遂成通行的分期框架，雖然更早的掠奪與更晚的北歐王國並不在此框架之內。實際的變化有三層。第一層在英格蘭：修道院在島上的常駐形勢無法維持，修會向本寧一帶後撤，島上據點改由世俗力量看守，沿海防禦自此不再依靠修士而依靠城堡與艦隊；西撒克遜方面到阿爾弗雷德時代才造出大型戰船，並以「市鎮堡壘」體系把海岸線變成可防守的序列。第二層在北歐：劫掠的收益證明海上戰爭有利可圖，催生規模更大的船隊與更嚴格的戰利品分贓制度；72 年後「偉大異教軍」以數萬之眾橫掃英格蘭的編制與效率，正是在這類經驗上累積而成。第三層在教會與文化：聖物與書冊的散失迫使修院重抄經卷，愛爾蘭與北歐因襲擊而結成的修道院網絡被沖擊多次，沿海修道院體系的崩潰在 9 世紀初一度令整個西歐教會震動，而 1066 年的斯檀福橋是這條線索的終點。北歐自身也在劫掠與傳教之間擺動，數十年後的哈拉爾德·哈德拉達正是同一條跨境航線的後繼者。
impactEn: In later memory the year 793 was fixed as the beginning of the Viking Age, and the span 793 to 1066 became the usual framework of the period, even though earlier raids and later Scandinavian kingdoms both fall outside it. The real changes run on three levels. The first is in England: the monastery could no longer be held permanently on the island, the community withdrew to the Bamburgh area, and the island position passed to secular watch, so that coastal defence from then on rested on castles and fleets rather than on monks; in the West Saxon kingdom large warships were not built until the age of Alfred, and the burh system turned the coastline into a defensible sequence. The second is in the North: the profits of plunder demonstrated that war at sea paid, and produced larger fleets and stricter rules for dividing the spoil; the organisation and efficiency with which the Great Heathen Army swept through England seventy-two years later was built precisely on experiences of this kind. The third is in the Church and in culture: the scattering of shrines and books forced monasteries to copy their texts afresh, the network of Irish and Scandinavian houses joined together by trade and pilgrimage was struck repeatedly, and the collapse of the coastal monastic system shook the Latin Church across western Europe in the early ninth century; the bridge at Stamford in 1066 is the end of that thread. The North itself swung between plunder and preaching, and Harald Hardrada, decades later, was the successor on the very same cross-border route.
result: 結果是攻方得手、守方未潰、事件未了。一側：林迪斯法恩的圍院與教堂被攻破，金銀器皿、聖物匣、織物與書冊被搬上船，修士團遭到殺傷並被驅散，著名的卡爾特座椅據說被帶往北方，後來才得回；修士在海峽一線的教堂重建被視為此役的實際終點。另一側：諾森布里亞王的追兵在退潮灘地與登陸的船隊短兵相接，依編年史記載收回部分財物，但潮水回漲使襲擊者帶著贓物安全離開，沒有一艘船被攔下，編年史也沒有記錄防守方有重大傷亡。整場戰役因此既不是殲滅戰，也不是守城戰，而是一次成功的、以潮汐為界線的有限目標掠奪：攻方帶走物資退入北海，守方保住島嶼卻失去重複的財富與名聲。此後的意義在時間軸上：793 之後至 878 年前北歐大軍三次深入英格蘭，886 年起維京人溯泰晤士河而上並以長船逼入倫敦，直到 878 年阿爾弗雷德於埃丁頓取勝、894 年血斧埃里克被逐出本寧，這一整條戰爭線才告收束；島上那座石頭堡壘直到 16 世紀才蓋成，但修道院遺址至今仍立在退潮時可涉水到達的沙洲旁。
resultEn: The result was that the attackers won, the defenders were not broken, and the affair was left unfinished. On one side, the enclosure and church of Lindisfarne were broken into, the gold and silver plate, reliquaries, textiles and books were carried up to the ships, the monastic community was struck down and scattered, and the famous chair of St Cuthbert was said to have been carried away north and only later returned; the rebuilding of the church on the mainland side of the strait is generally treated as the practical end of the episode. On the other side, the king's pursuers came into contact with the landed crews on the ebb-tide flats and, according to the chronicle, recovered part of the property; but the returning tide let the raiders sail off with their plunder, not one ship was intercepted, and the chronicle records no serious loss on the defensive side. The whole action was therefore neither a decisive battle nor a siege defence, but a successful, tide-limited raid on a finite objective: the attackers took their haul and withdrew into the North Sea, while the defenders kept the island but lost the wealth and the standing they had held. What matters is what followed: between 793 and 878 Scandinavian armies entered England three times, from 886 the Vikings rowed up the Thames and brought longships to London, and only with Alfred's victory at Edington in 878 and the expulsion of Erik Bloodaxe from Bamburgh in 894 was that whole line of war closed. The stone fortress on the island was not built until the sixteenth century, yet the ruins of the priory still stand beside the sandbank that can be walked to at low water.
